newsitem.title: ITALY: Draft mini-budget now, decide later - Italy's Ciampi.
newsitem.headline: Draft mini-budget now, decide later - Italy's Ciampi.

text.p: Italy should begin drafting a mini-budget for 1997 and decide later whether it needs to implement it, Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said.
"Let's prepare ourselves to do one and then we'll decide whether in fact it is necessary," Il Sole 24 Ore on Friday quoted Ciampi as telling a parliamentary budget commission.

Analysts say an overshoot in the 1996 public sector borrowing requirement has left a hole in state accounts and say the government will have to implement a supplementary budget of up to 25 trillion lire as early as next month to plug the gap.
Italy ran up a public sector deficit of 138.5 trillion lire last year compared with an original target of 109.4 trillion.
Economists believe the 1997 austerity budget, cutting 62.5 trillion lire off the deficit, may not be enough for Italy to join a European single currency at the planned start in 1999.

The government has said it will not know the full impact of the PSBR overshoot on 1997 accounts until the second half of February. Prime Minister Romano Prodi has said he wants to wait for official state accounts before deciding on a mini-budget.
